newsitem.title: USA: U S West agrees to pay pension fund $8 mln.
newsitem.headline: U S West agrees to pay pension fund $8 mln.

text.p: U S West Inc agreed on Monday to pay $8 million to one of its pension funds to settle a 1994 lawsuit that accused the company of improperly charging administration expenses to the fund, according to a written agreement.

In the settlement document, which was obtained by Reuters, U S West denied any wrongdoing. A spokeswoman for the company said the document was expected to be filed with the court before the close of the day on Monday.
The company will make the $8 million payment directly into the pension fund and not to individual retirees, according to the agreement.
The lawsuit, filed in U.S. District Court in Denver, claimed the expenses should have been assumed by U S West.
U S West earlier said it had been authorized to charge the expenses to the pension fund.
In the original lawsuit, which had been granted class-action status, plaintiffs claimed U S West improperly charged about $30 million to the fund. But the figure was later reduced to $10 million.
The charges in question covered legal, consulting, and payroll expenses for administering the pension fund.
The settlement must still be approved by a federal judge.
In the agreement U S West said the pension fund was "very well funded and very well managed."
